elements.quote: Healthcare accreditation evaluates hospitals against established standards to promote continuous quality improvement. However, its long-term effectiveness on healthcare quality and patient satisfaction remains debatable
elements.reason: Describes current knowledge about accreditation and highlights uncertainties in long-term effectiveness.

elements.quote: highlighting the need for enhanced standards and stakeholder support. This study evaluated the impact of healthcare accreditation on quality outcomes across diverse hospital settings.

elements.quote: Outcome commensurability for the meta-analysis was defined a priori as: (i) measurement of the same construct (healthcare-quality score derived from accreditation-aligned domains - patient safety, organizational performance, and quality of care); (ii) reporting of effect on continuous scale convertible to standardized mean difference (SMD); and (iii) availability of pre-and post-accreditation comparator data, or accredited vs. non-accredited group comparison, with sample sizes and dispersion statistics. Studies that reported the construct only qualitatively, used non-convertible categorical outcomes, or lacked dispersion statistics were excluded from pooling and analysed narratively.
